title: Spotting False Information
tagline: How to check if news and messages are true before you share.
description: Not everything forwarded on WhatsApp is true. Learn quick checks to tell real news from rumours, so you protect your family and community.
outcomes: Ask three questions before you share
Check who really sent a message
Spot edited photos and old videos
Find trusted news sources in Zambia
Talk to others kindly about false news

lessons.title: Three questions before you share
lessons.body:
Before you forward a message, ask three questions.

## Who sent it first?
A forward from a friend may have started with a stranger. Look for the real source.

## Is it on trusted news?
Check ZNBC, a trusted newspaper, or a community radio station you know.

## How does it make me feel?
Messages that make you very angry or scared are often made to spread fast. Slow down.
lessons.try_it: Take the last forwarded message you received and ask the three questions.

lessons.title: Old photos, new stories
lessons.body:
A common trick is using an old photo or video and saying it happened today.

## How to check
Look for clues: the weather, signs, clothing, phone models. Ask the sender where it came from. If no one knows, do not share.
key_points: Photos can be old or edited
Look for clues in the picture
lessons.try_it: Find a photo in a group chat and look for clues about when it was taken.

lessons.title: Practice: check a message
lessons.body:
Here is a message: "Government is giving K2,000 to every family. Click this link and enter your NRC number before Friday!"

## Think it through
There is a deadline, a link, a request for your NRC number and free money. These are four warning signs. Real government programmes are announced on official channels and do not ask for your details by link.
key_points: Free money plus a link is a warning
Never send your NRC number by link
lessons.try_it: Share what you learned with one person in your family.

quiz.question: A message makes you very angry. What is the best first step?
quiz.explanation: Messages that cause strong feelings are often made to spread. Slow down and check first.

quiz.question: A message offers free money if you enter your NRC number at a link. This is:
options: Safe if a friend sent it
quiz.explanation: Free money, a deadline, a link and a request for your NRC are all warning signs.
